Consider the determinant of the identity matrix $$I = \left[\begin{array}{rr} 1\amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{rr} \evec_1 \amp \evec_2 \\ \end{array}\right] $$ . As seen on the left of [fig-det-identity], the vectors $\vvec_1 = \evec_1$ and $\vvec_2=\evec_2$ form a positively oriented pair. Since the parallelogram they form is a $1\times1$ square, we have $\det(I) = 1.$

The determinant $\det(I) = 1$, as seen on the left. On the right, we see that $\det(A) = -2$ where $A$ is the matrix whose columns are shown.

Now consider the matrix $$A = \left[\begin{array}{rr} -2\amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{rr} \vvec_1 \amp \vvec_2 \\ \end{array}\right] $$ . As seen on the right of [fig-det-identity], the vectors $\vvec_1$ and $\vvec_2$ form a negatively oriented pair. The parallelogram they define is a $2\times1$ rectangle so we have $\det(A) = -2$.
